body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Sunday, August 16, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a high of 98°, a low of 72°, and air quality at a moderate 58. Our top story this morning is a tragic wrong-way crash on Highway 99 that left three people dead. Let’s get you caught up on the night and the week ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

The night brought a mix of serious incidents and routine calls across Kern County. The most significant event was a vehicle fire and extrication on southbound Highway 99 north of 7th Standard Road around 1 a.m. A subject was pinned and unconscious in the vehicle, and crews worked to cut away the fire and extricate two patients, both of whom were able to walk (green tag). Also around the county, a possible shooting call had units staging on Price Street before 10 p.m., though no confirmed shots were heard. A DUI driver in a white BMW fled east from the 33rd Street area just after midnight. And in southeast Bakersfield, a palm tree fire climbed into the roof of a two-story apartment complex on Spice Way, drawing a reinforced response with Engine 7 as incident commander. Elsewhere, officers handled a long string of domestics and disturbances, including one at a Camellia Village apartment where a hole was punched in the wall.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 98° and a low around 72° tonight. It’s currently 84° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is moderate at an AQI of 58.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that three people are dead after a wrong-way, three-vehicle crash on Highway 99 early Sunday morning.** According to California Highway Patrol Bakersfield, a white Honda Accord was traveling northbound in the southbound lanes on Highway 99, north of 7th Standard Road, when it collided with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado around 12:44 a.m. The crash caused the Honda to catch fire, and all three occupants inside died from their injuries. The driver and one other occupant of the BMW sustained major injuries, while the two occupants in the Chevrolet had minor injuries. Officials say it is unknown whether alcohol or drugs were a factor in the crash.

**KGET 17 says that a man was arrested in a Bakersfield domestic violence standoff involving minors.** Bakersfield Police Department officials told KGET that the incident unfolded in a neighborhood where a man had barricaded himself inside a home with children present. The arrest followed a standoff situation, though no further details on the circumstances or the suspect’s identity were immediately available.

**Bakersfield Now tells us that the 90s are back as a Pacific trough brings "cooler" highs to Kern County.** After a recent heatwave, the region is seeing a slight dip in temperatures, with forecasts indicating that the upcoming week will bring highs in the 90s rather than the triple digits experienced earlier. This shift is attributed to a Pacific trough moving into the area, offering some relief from the intense summer heat.

**23ABC shares that Bakersfield police and fire chiefs presented their Fourth of July findings at a Friday meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city.** Bakersfield Fire Chief Kevin Albertson noted that the holiday brought serious consequences statewide, with people significantly injured or killed by fireworks. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined. Fire-related responses dropped 6% compared to 2025, but officials and residents agree that more work remains to deter illegal fireworks use.

## Something good

Kern County’s own Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, recently traveled to San Diego to celebrate the public release of a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community—a project he helped build from the ground up. Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the nation’s drug czar to develop the toolkit. This initiative highlights the local community’s contribution to addressing addiction on a broader scale.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, several public meetings and events are on the calendar for Kern County. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m., followed by the Historic Preservation Commission at 4:00 p.m. and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2:00 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board convenes at 10:00 a.m. Later in the week, the Planning Commission meets on Thursday, August 20, at 5:30 p.m. 

For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a lineup of shows starting with Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio on August 22. Rodney Carrington takes the stage on August 27, followed by CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28. Willie Barcena performs on August 29, and a Michael Jackson tribute featuring Michael Phoenix is also scheduled for August 29. Rounding out the month, the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA comes to the Fox on September 4. 

That’s your Sunday brief. Stay cool, and have a great week ahead.
